subject: Reconciliation request: duplicate ledger posting on May invoices
messages:
From: Katie Jenkins <katie.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected charges on May invoices - possible duplicate posting

Hi Marissa,

We were reconciling May and noticed two identical line items for 2027-05-01 (Invoice #ACM-2027-05-01) that look like a duplicate posting: one for $16,000 and another identical $16,000 charge on the same invoice sequence. Our AP team has put the payment on hold until we can sort this out.

I've attached a screenshot of our payment rail showing the two captures (payment_screenshot.png). We also need clarification on how VAT was applied — our UK entity provided VAT ID GB999888555 and the invoice shows VAT added on both lines, which doubles the VAT amount payable.

Could you confirm whether this is an overcharge and what remediation you can offer? We are close to our renewal and would like to get this settled quickly.

Thanks,
Katie Jenkins
Head of Finance, ACME Inc.
katie.jenkins@acme.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachment: payment_screenshot.png (image/png)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Jenkins <katie.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges on May invoices - possible duplicate posting

Hi Katie — thanks for flagging this and for the screenshot. I’m very sorry for the confusion and the payment hold — we’ll prioritize this.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I’ve pulled the invoice PDF (ACME_Inc_invoice_2027-05-01.pdf) and I can see the duplicate line item.
- I’ve looped in Finance (Ben) and Billing Ops (Naomi) to validate the ledger entries and calculate the right remediation amount.
- If this is an accidental double-post, we will issue a credit memo and an amended invoice that correctly reflects the VAT treatment for your UK VAT ID.

Could you please forward your VAT certificate for ACME UK (GB999888555) or confirm if you want us to zero-rate the invoice under reverse charge? If you can attach that to a reply it will speed the reissue.

I’ll follow up internally and aim to send a proposed credit and amended invoice by end of day tomorrow. Apologies again for the disruption.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(Attachment: ACME_Inc_invoice_2027-05-01.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected charges on May invoices - duplicate posting (ACME / D-47821)

Team — forwarding ACME’s ticket. Key details: duplicate line for $16,000, VAT applied twice, customer has UK VAT ID GB999888555 and has paused payment. Attachments from customer and the invoice are attached.

Naomi — can you confirm whether this was a billing system replay/ingest duplication or a client-side duplicate subscription charge? Ben — if it’s our double-post, propose we issue a goodwill credit for the full duplicated net amount ($16,000) plus correction of the VAT line (refund of VAT on the duplicated line). I’ve started a quick calc in the attached sheet (calculation_sheet_20270610.csv).

Suggested approach:
- If finance signs off, issue a credit memo for $19,200 (duplicated net + VAT) and reissue an amended invoice showing the correct single line and VAT treatment.
- Offer a one-time courtesy credit of $1,000 toward their July invoice given the disruption to AP workflow (helps preserve the renewal).
- Request VAT certificate from ACME so we can apply reverse charge/zero-rate if applicable — saves them from paying VAT twice while we correct ledger entries.

Logan — if this requires a ledger write-off or manual journal entry, please advise the GL code and expected timing so I can set expectations with the customer.

Thanks — Marissa
(Attachment: calculation_sheet_20270610.csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Jenkins <katie.jenkins@acme.com>, ACME Inc. Billing <billing@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 17:34:00 -0700
Subject: Resolution proposal and next steps – duplicate posting on May invoice (ACME / D-47821)

Hi Katie — thanks for your patience while we investigated this. Here’s what we found and the remediation we’re proposing: 

What happened:
- A backend ingestion error resulted in a duplicate ledger posting for Invoice #ACM-2027-05-01. The same subscription line was recorded twice, which also caused VAT to appear on both lines.

What we’re doing: 
1) Issuing a credit memo for the duplicated net charge ($16,000) plus VAT on that line ($3,200) — total credit $19,200. Credit memo attached (credit_memo_20270614.pdf).
2) Reissuing an amended invoice for the net single line with correct VAT handling (amended_invoice_20270614.pdf).
3) Providing a one-time courtesy credit of $1,000 applied to your July invoice as a gesture for the AP disruption.
4) If you prefer reverse charge/zero-rate treatment we will reissue without VAT once we receive your UK VAT certificate; please reply with the certificate if you want that option.
5) Expected timing: credit will post in our billing system within 3 business days; the refund (if already paid twice) or applied credit will reflect on your account statement thereafter. If you need a wire refund instead of account credit, confirm and we’ll open the refund workflow (may take 5–7 business days after approval).

Links and attachments: credit_memo_20270614.pdf (credit memo), amended_invoice_20270614.pdf (amended invoice), HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-47821, DocuSign for acceptance: https://www.docusign.com/ABC123-ACME-credit-accept

Next steps for ACME: please confirm which of the following you prefer:
- Apply credit to outstanding balance and proceed with single-payment settlement once posted.
- Request wire refund for the duplicated amount (include wire details).
- Send VAT certificate for reverse charge reissue (if you want VAT zero-rated).

Once we have your preference I’ll finalize the credit and amended invoice. Again, apologies for the error and the trouble it caused your AP team.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
